title: Argosy Health - Escalation Postmortem Follow-up
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-11-23 10:30 PST | Duration approx 45m | Attendees: Janelle Park (Redwood AE), Marco Silva (Redwood SE), Deena Rao (Redwood CSM), Priya Shah (Argosy Dir Infra), Liam O'Connor (CTO), Samir Patel (SRE)

Summary: short follow-up on last week's incident where serving pool flapped during a config rollout, led to elevated latencies and 5xx errors for ~28 minutes; review of root cause, mitigation already applied, next mitigations and runbook actions, scheduling reliability tests and proof points for Dedicated vs Hosted options.

Topics: [postmortem recap, root cause, immediate mitigation, permanent mitigations, monitoring/alerts, runbook & playbooks, next steps, stakeholders and timeline]

[00:00] Janelle: hey everyone thanks for carving out time, we wanted to run through the postmortem, confirm mitigations, and make sure the runbook covers what you need. quick check, is this recording ok for notes?
[00:16] Priya: yes thanks Janelle, we got the initial postmortem but wanted to talk through a couple follow-ups: the autoscale settings, and the fallbacks that didn't trigger as expected.
[00:28] Marco: yeah quick recap from our side — root cause summary: during the 2:00 AM config rollout a traffic-splitting rule intended to move 10% to new kernel paths had a bad selector, which caused a subset of requests to hit an incompatible quantized model variant. that caused higher memory pressure and KV cache thrashing, which cascaded into higher tail latency and several request timeouts.
[00:52] Liam: just to clarify, the issue was the selector not matching the node labels so the router fell back incorrectly?
[00:58] Marco: sort of, the router did the fallback but the fallback path used a model variant that didn't have the same cache warm state — so you got cold KV cache and we saw a burst of long-latency requests; also the autoscaler had a minimum pod count set lower than the real traffic floor so it couldn't scale fast enough from the burst.
[01:22] Samir: yep we saw the error rate spike at 01:54 and our alert threshold for 5xx was configured at 10%, which only alerted after the second minute, and by then several upstream jobs re-tried and made things worse.
[01:36] Deena: action there was we rolled back the config and disabled the rollout, and Janelle pushed a temporary policy to pin traffic to the previously verified model variant. that dropped 5xxs within about five minutes.
[01:52] Priya: that rollback was good, thanks. but two holes: one, our route-level circuit breaker didn't trip (it was lower than needed) and two, our tracing didn't include the model variant label so it's hard to correlate requests to the faulty variant in our logs.
[02:08] Marco: noted. for tracing we recommended adding the model-variant tag to the request spans, and for the circuit breaker we proposed raising the early threshold and adding a token-bucket limiter at the edge.
[02:22] Janelle: and on the Redwood side we already made three changes: 1) bumped min pool size for that region for Argosy's tenant, 2) added a rollback guard to prevent that specific selector mismatch from rolling out without an allowlist, 3) added an alert that watches for KV cache miss ratio spikes.
[02:40] Liam: can you confirm the K M S / H S M stuff we talked about — sorry ASR ate it last time — we want to make sure encryption changes weren't impacted.
[02:50] Marco: yes encryption keys were never rotated during the rollout; KMS (the customer's KMS) remained intact. the only thing that changed was model variant selection, not key material. apol — apols for the transcription noise earlier, but there was no K M S change.
[03:04] Priya: ok good. one more: are there plans to add a canary verification that includes synthetic traffic to warm the KV cache before shifting production traffic?
[03:12] Marco: absolutely, proposed mitigation is a pre-rollout warm step — send a small set of synthetic prefix traffic to populate KV for the new variant and validate tail latency SLOs for 5 minutes before increasing traffic. we'll add that to the rollout pipeline.
[03:28] Samir: we also want a documented runbook for our on-call: steps to toggle traffic, how to pin to previous variant, what alerts to expect, and exact runbook commands.
[03:36] Deena: we'll own the runbook template, Redwood will provide the RW commands and we will embed them.

[10:12] Marco: some additional details from logs: we saw KV cache miss ratio jump to ~82% for affected pods, p95 latency from 150ms to 1.8s, and a correlated CPU jump due to repeated decoder kernels thrashing memory. this is consistent with a model variant mismatch + cold state.
[10:40] Liam: are there long-term mitigations to prevent this class of problem? is it config management, or runtime safety?
[10:48] Marco: both. config-level: schema validation and selector allowlists (we already merged a PR for that). runtime-level: we want prefix warming, circuit breakers, and better autoscale policies tuned to Argosy's traffic patterns (shorter scale-up windows and a higher minimum).
[11:10] Janelle: also adding an automatic fallback that only routes to variants that have a fully warmed cache within the last hour. if warming hasn't been observed then the router skips that variant.

[18:05] Priya: question on observability: can you add model-variant to cost and token-level breakdown we see in Cortex? we need to be able to query by variant in the console or via API.
[18:18] Marco: yes that's on our roadmap; short-term we'll add tags to telemetry and provide a queryable field in the logs and metrics.

[22:30] Samir: on SLA / contract impact — our ops team wants a postmortem that shows corrective actions and timeline before continuing with the next scheduled rollout; we also want a reliability test showing no regressions.
[22:44] Deena: we'll get the formal postmortem doc to you by EOD tomorrow with timeline and root cause detail, and we'll schedule a joint load test next week.

[28:00] Janelle: ok to walk through the proposed action list?
[28:08] Marco: sure. 1) add model-variant tags to spans & logs; 2) implement pre-rollout KV-warm step; 3) raise circuit-breaker thresholds and add token-bucket limiter at edge; 4) increase min pool size and shorten autoscale window; 5) add rollback guard allowlist; 6) update alerts to lower detection latency and include cache-miss ratio; 7) formal runbook & playbook.
[28:36] Priya: sounds good — for 4 we want to understand cost impact; if raising min pool size affects billing significantly we need a business case.
[28:46] Marco: we'll provide estimated token / GPU-hour delta for the change, and Redwood Optimize will run a quick simulation for cost delta.

[34:10] Liam: competitors — not our main focus but for procurement notes, we did look at Mistral Cloud's managed endpoints and also an in-house solution. they handled warming differently, but there were tradeoffs on price and control.
[34:28] Janelle: noted, we'll include a short comparison doc in the follow-up.

[39:50] Priya: timeline — we need the runbook and postmortem by tomorrow EOD, the KV warm pre-rollout in staging by next Wednesday, and a reliability load test with Redwood present the following week.
[40:06] Deena: we'll schedule the load test for Thursday next week and invite your SREs.
[40:14] Samir: final ask — can Redwood run the warm step in staging and provide telemetry to us so we can see the warm success before rolling in prod?
[40:24] Marco: yes we'll run it and share the traces and cache-miss graphs.
[40:32] Janelle: ok quick recap on next steps and owners now...
[40:36] Janelle: Deena will send the formal postmortem doc (owner: Deena Rao) by 2026-11-24 EOD.
[40:44] Deena: yes I'll send it, includes timeline, root cause, mitigations, rollback steps.
[40:48] Janelle: Marco to add model-variant tags and provide a telemetry patch and sample queries by 2026-11-25.
[40:58] Marco: yep will do.
[41:00] Janelle: Marco/Eng to implement pre-rollout KV-warm in staging and run the staged warm test by 2026-11-25, share results.
[41:12] Marco: ok.
[41:14] Priya: Argosy to review cost impact for increased min pool and confirm willingness to accept cost delta by 2026-11-27.
[41:24] Liam: we'll confirm after we see the Optimize simulation.
[41:30] Janelle: Deena to schedule joint load test Thursday 2026-12-03 and invite Argosy SREs.
[41:40] Deena: scheduled, invite to follow.
[41:44] Janelle: any other items?
[41:46] Priya: no that's it, appreciate the quick turnaround.
[41:50] Janelle: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with artifacts.

[45:00] End meeting
summary: Follow-up on Argosy Health escalation: root cause was model-variant rollout selector mismatch causing KV cache thrashing and autoscale constraints; temporary rollback resolved the incident. Agreed mitigations: prefix warming, model-variant tagging in telemetry, higher min pool size/shorter autoscale windows, circuit breakers, rollback guard allowlist, improved alerts and runbook. Owners and due dates assigned.
action_items: Deena Rao | Produce formal postmortem doc including timeline, root cause, mitigations, rollback steps | due: 2026-11-24
Marco Silva | Add model-variant tags to spans/logs and provide telemetry patch + sample queries | due: 2026-11-25
Marco Silva | Implement pre-rollout KV-warm in staging and run staged warm test, share results | due: 2026-11-25
Redwood Engineering | Provide estimated GPU-hour / cost delta for raising min pool size (via Redwood Optimize) | due: 2026-11-26
Deena Rao | Schedule joint load test and invite Argosy SREs | due: 2026-12-03

Implement telemetry & KV warm in staging and share results by 2026-11-25
